title: GitHub repository default-branch protection state
description: The effective protection of one repository's default branch, merged from classic branch protection and every active ruleset that applies to it. Supersedes github.repo_protection.v1, which reported an unreadable repository's fields as 0 and false, ignored rulesets, and had no stable repository id. A protection field the connector could not read is omitted, never reported as off. 2.1.0 adds the required status checks, whether force pushes are allowed, the repository topics and whether the repository deploys to production.

repo_id.description: GitHub's repository id. Stable across renames; checks key on it.

required_reviews.description: The highest required approving review count across classic protection and active rulesets.

enforce_admins.description: A source that requires an approving review binds admins: classic enforce_admins, or a ruleset none of whose bypass actors can be an admin (only an app or a deploy key may bypass). Omitted when that rests on a ruleset whose bypass actors the token can't read.

required_status_checks.description: Every required status check context, from classic protection and every active required_status_checks rule, sorted. Empty when no source requires one.

allow_force_pushes.description: Force pushes to the branch are allowed: false when classic protection disables them or a non_fast_forward rule blocks them. Who may bypass the block is not read. Omitted when classic protection does not report allow_force_pushes and no rule decides it.

topics.description: The repository's topics, from the organization repository listing. Present even when the protection could not be read; omitted when the listing does not report them.

deploys_to_production.description: The topics include the connector's production topic (--production-topic, default production). Omitted exactly when topics is.

protection_source.description: Where the branch's protection comes from.

reason.description: Why the connector's verdict is what it is; for an inconclusive record, what could not be read.
